required.description: Managers' scheduled posts wait for approval.

example: Roast date on every bag. Not a best-by.

topUpBalance.description: Credits from top-up packs (don't expire monthly).

MentionCandidate.description: Someone who can see the post and may be @mentioned in a note.

PlatformAccountIds.description: Per-platform account targeting. Each value is either a single socialAccounts doc id (single-account targeting, legacy/Zapier callers) or an array of ids (multi-account targeting — publish to N accounts on that platform in one call). Use the `id` values from GET /social-accounts, not usernames. Required for any non-draft post on a platform with more than one connected account; with exactly one, it may be omitted.

PlatformMediaIndexes.description: Image posts only: which images each platform gets, as zero-based positions in the post's media list (media, mediaIds, or libraryItemId). Platforms not listed get every image; an empty list sends that platform none. Useful because X and Bluesky post at most 4 images. On update, null resets to every image everywhere, and replacing media without this field clears the picks.

PlatformMetadata.description: Optional per-platform metadata. Each sub-key is only relevant when that platform is present in `platforms`; all sub-keys and their fields are optional.

boardId.description: Board id to pin to. Boards live under a specific Pinterest account, so this only works when a single Pinterest account is targeted. For multi-account Pinterest posts, use `boardIdByAccount` instead.

boardIdByAccount.description: Per-account board selection: socialAccounts doc id → Pinterest board id. Required when more than one Pinterest account is targeted on the post, since the same board id doesn't resolve across accounts.

tiktok.description: TikTok publishing options. With privacy_level set, the post publishes directly to the profile. Without it, the post uploads to the creator's TikTok inbox as a draft.

allow_duet.description: Allow Duet (video only). Off when omitted.

allow_stitch.description: Allow Stitch (video only). Off when omitted.

branded_content.description: Promotes a third party. TikTok labels it "Paid partnership". Can't be SELF_ONLY.

commercial_content_toggle.description: Disclose that the post promotes a brand, product, or service. When true, set your_brand, branded_content, or both.

privacy_level.description: Who can view the post. Setting it publishes directly to the TikTok profile (Direct Post). Omit it to upload an inbox draft that the creator finishes in the TikTok app. It must be one of the account's current privacy options. Branded content can't be SELF_ONLY. Accounts connected before Direct Post was enabled get an inbox draft until they reconnect.

your_brand.description: Promotes the creator's own business. TikTok labels it "Promotional content".

privacyStatus.description: Requested YouTube video visibility. YouTube may restrict uploads from unaudited API projects to private.

brandId.description: Working brand. Equals the user id for the default brand. Omitted on documents written before brand scoping.

caption.example: Big day ahead. Here we go.

libraryItemId.description: Single media item attached to this post.

replyTo.description: External tweet ID this post is replying to (for Twitter threads). Single-account threading only.

results.description: Per-platform delivery outcomes. Absent until the post has been through a publish attempt.

PostApproval.description: Approval request and decision, on brands that require approval.

nextCursor.description: Pass back as `?cursor=` to fetch the next page.

PostNote.description: Internal note on a post. Never published.

mentions.description: Teammates @mentioned in this note. Each was notified.

PostResult.description: How one platform (and account) handled this post.

accountId.description: socialAccounts doc id, when the post recorded one.

error.example: TikTok rejected the upload: this account has hit TikTok's daily post limit

failReason.description: The platform's own machine-readable cause, when it names one. Stable enough to branch on.

postId.description: The platform's id for the delivered post, or its async job id while pending.

status.description: `pending` means the platform accepted the job and has not returned a terminal answer yet. It resolves on its own within a few minutes — poll this endpoint rather than republishing, which would deliver the post twice.

url.description: Public URL to the post, when the platform gives one.

PostStatus.description: `partial` means at least one platform accepted the post and at least one did not — inspect `distributionStatus` for the per-platform outcome. `pending_approval` means a teammate scheduled it on a brand that requires approval; it is not delivered until approved (see approvePost).

angles.description: Distinct reasons to buy, each a possible ad concept.

hooks.description: Opening lines for short product videos.

images.description: Product photos saved to the media library. Use a mediaId as libraryItemId to animate it.

url.description: The product page it was imported from.

Recurrence.description: Repeat rule for a scheduled post. Only the next occurrence exists at a time: when one is picked up for delivery, the next is created as a new scheduled post with the same content. Times repeat on the wall clock in `timeZone`, so DST does not shift them. Set it to null on update to stop repeating.

index.description: 0-based position in the series; set by the server.

seriesId.description: Shared by every occurrence; set by the server.

until.description: Last allowed occurrence date (YYYY-MM-DD) in timeZone.

ReportSchedule.description: A brand's scheduled client report email.

commentary.description: Notes printed at the end of every report.

creditsRefunded.description: Credits returned for ads that failed.

status.description: `ready` when at least one ad was made; check each variant's status. `failed` when none were, with every credit refunded.

headline.description: The line drawn on the image.

mediaId.description: Finished image in the media library.

postId.description: Draft post for this ad, ready to schedule.

UsageBreakdown.description: Shared account allowances with per-brand attribution. Limits are not split per brand.

minutesUsedPeriod.description: Processing credits consumed this period for this brand.

storageBytes.description: Library and clip bytes attributed to this brand.

actualModel.description: Model executing the current attempt; omni-1-2 when fallback is used.

creditsCharged.description: Final charge: equals creditsReserved when ready, 0 when failed (refunded), null while running.

creditsReserved.description: Credits taken when the job started.

fallbackUsed.description: Whether Omni 1.2 replaced the requested model. The original quoted credits stay unchanged; no second charge.

mediaId.description: Library item id once ready. Attach it to posts.

signingSecret.description: HMAC-SHA256 signing secret. Shown ONCE at creation. Use to verify payloads via the X-Viralnote-Signature header.

apiKeyAuth.description: API key created at https://dashboard.viralnote.app/developers/auth. Keys are scoped at creation; the scope each operation needs is listed in its `security` entry under `oauth2`. The same key may be sent as `Authorization: Bearer vnd_...`.

post.description: Each variant: a distinct hook and angle, AI shots (3 shared plus a hook shot, 5s each), a Gemini voiceover, captions burned in the brand style, the logo, and a draft post with per-platform captions plus paid-ad copy. Credits = shots × the model's per-second rate × 5 + 3 per variant (e.g. kling-3, 3 variants: 6 × 15 + 9 = 99). Estimate first with `POST /credits/estimate` `{ kind: "ad" }`. The full amount is taken when the job starts and is the most it will cost; the request fails with `insufficient-credits` if the balance can't cover it. If the ad fails, credits for anything unfinished are refunded. Failed b-roll shots may fall back to Omni 1.2 at the original quoted price without charging again; presenter lip-sync is excluded. Nothing is published automatically. AI can get logos, product details, claims and captions wrong, so have a person watch each draft with sound before publishing it.
